To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the loss landscapes of DNNs have a structure that is fundamentally different from other non-convex optimization problems, and that this structure is the result of a natural regularization that arises from training DNNs.
1. We prove that the loss landscape "contains" all critical points of narrower DNNs, and this structure is starkly different to that of protein-folding and other nonconvex optimization problems.
1. We propose an embedding principle that any critical point/affinity subspace of a narrower D NN can be embedded to any wider D NN with higher degeneracies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new class of problems, which we call the "embedding problems".
understanding the structure of loss landscapes of deep neural networks and its implication.

the embedding principle of the loss landscape of deep networks is a very interesting and important concept that can be used to explain many aspects of deep learning, including the ease of optimization, the ability of generalization, and the implicit regularization of deep networks.

the loss landscape is not as complicated as it is often thought. It has some nice structures that can be exploited for understanding and designing better algorithms for training neural networks.
